**Jaina elements** in the storyline (e.g. the Jain nun Kavunthi Adigal)

0.x: The five Tamil epics (post-Sangam, c. 4th–6th c. CE)
**Twin epics** of early Tamil literature = **Silappadikaram and Manimekalai**.

r: **Tolkappiyam** by **Tolkappiyar** – the **oldest extant Tamil grammar**, a work on **grammar and poetics**
The only surviving work of the **Second Sangam**
**Tirukkural (Kural)** by **Tiruvalluvar** – **Tamil**, **1,330 couplets** on philosophy and ethics
About **2,400 poems** by some 450 poets, about 30 of them **women** (Avvaiyar the most prolific)
**Varna was known** to Sangam poets, though society was not rigidly stratified; rich in **material culture** and **warrior ethic**
The poems describe ports and goods but are **silent on the trade routes**; the **Milindapanha** and **Jatakas** describe routes
Sangam poet who refers to the **Mauryan expedition** against a Tamil chieftain

2.x: **Melkanakku** = Ettuthogai + Pattupattu = the **18 major** works; both are divided into **aham and puram**.
The aham and puram poems of the Padinenkilkanakku **continue** Sangam composition, which is why they are classed as **post-Sangam** works as against the Sangam works proper.

Accepted span **c. 300 BCE – 300 CE**; **Tamil-Brahmi** of the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early limit. The Tirukkural, the epics and the Pathinenkilkanakku are **post-Sangam**, not the earliest layer.

3.x: **Sangam** = an **assembly of Tamil poets** ("Conference of Poets"), held under **Pandya** patronage. The tradition comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul**; the account is traditional, not historical.

r: **Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, Keralaputras** as southern neighbours

Sangam urban site, contemporary with the Gangetic **Second Urbanisation**
